Spinner

A sign that something is in progress when how long it will take is not known.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • While a view or part of one loads and nothing can be shown yet.
  • While a background step runs, such as cloning a repository or running tests, beside the name of the step.

When not to use it

  • Inside a button that is working. Set aria-busy="true" on the button, which draws its own.
  • When the amount done is known. Use a progress element.
  • When the shape of the content is known and it will arrive within a moment. Show the layout with its text missing, not a spinner.
  • For anything that takes less than about a second. Show nothing.

Sizes

default
A 16px mark with text at the interface size. Inside a list, a panel or a row.
large gw-spinner--large
A 24px mark with 16px text. When a whole view is loading.

Accessibility

  • The text inside the spinner is its label. Name what is in progress, such as Loading runs. There is no spinner without text.
  • Set role="status" on the spinner so a screen reader announces the text when the app adds it.
  • When the text changes with each step, such as Cloning then Installing, keep one role="status" element in the page and change its text. Each change is announced.
  • Remove the spinner when the work ends. If it failed, put an error state or an alert in its place.
  • The mark is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup. It stops turning under prefers-reduced-motion, and the text still says what is happening.
  • A spinner is not focusable. An action that stops the work is a separate button beside it.

Classes

  • gw-spinner
  • gw-spinner--large
